name: Minimally invasive right-sided thoracic approach (T4–T10)
corridor: Same mini-thoracotomy plus viewing and retraction portals as the left-sided T10–L2 window, used on the right for T4–T10

positioning.text: Position for a right chest approach. The left-sided T10–L2 chapter states that T4–T10 is approached from the right and T10–L2 from the left, according to aortic anatomy.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the fractured vertebra on the right chest. Portal geometry matches the left mini-thoracic window: viewing portal two spaces cranial, retraction portal one space cranial and about 10 cm anterior.

incision.text: Mini-thoracotomy over the marked vertebra, with additional 20 mm portals entering above the rib.

superficial_interval.text: Take intercostal muscle off the cranial rib, open pleura, inspect with a thoracoscope, then place further portals under vision.

deep_interval.text: Open parietal pleura over the discs at the target and one level above and below, manage segmental vessels, and expose to the ALL and rib heads as on the left.

layers.text: Skin, chest wall, pleural cavity, parietal pleura, then the right side of T4–T10.

structures_at_risk.text: Lung, intercostal bundle, segmental vessels, and the great vessels; the thoracic duct is a right-sided concern in this field.

danger_zones.text: Entering below the rib and working without protecting mediastinal vessels are the danger zones.

retraction_hazards.text: Inflate the lung under thoracoscopic vision before removing the last portal.

exposure.text: Shows T4–T10 from a mini-open right thoracotomy.

limitations.text: Not the preferred side for T10–L2, where a left window is used because of the aorta.

indications.text: Used for minimally invasive right thoracic access from T4 to T10.

closure.text: Close as for the left mini-thoracic window, with chest drains through the portals.

complications.text: Complications include lung injury, intercostal-bundle injury, and thoracic-duct injury.

procedure_applications.condition: A T4–T10 fracture is instrumented through a mini-open right thoracotomy

questions.question: Which thoracic levels are approached from the right in the mini-open system?
questions.answer: T4–T10, with T10–L2 typically left-sided because of the aorta.
